messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT: P1 fired for billing-ingest — invoice reconciliation delta > 100k tokens across multiple customers. PD incident: https://pd.example.com/incidents/PD123456 :rotating_light:
pd-bot: Incident PD123456 created and escalated. Acknowledgement required by on-call.
alice (oncall): acked — I'm on it. grabbing logs + checking consumers. :eyes:
bob-sre: on standby. can you paste the PD link? also what region/cluster?
alice (oncall): PD link above. looks like billing-ingest-consumer group spiked lag on kafka-cluster-prod-2 in eu-west-1. first-pass numbers show ~120k token delta around 2026-03-12 02:00-03:00 UTC.
carol-billing: saw alerts from finance: some invoices scheduled for 2026-03-12 may undercount usage. holding invoice generation for affected accounts. please advise impact window.
dinesh-platform: tagging @bob-sre for consumer investigation. quick commands to check consumer lag:```bash
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka-cluster-prod-2:9093 --group billing-ingest-consumer --describe
```
bob-sre: running now. also checking the ingest worker logs for requeue/backpressure. quick check of consumer offsets:```text
GROUP                      TOPIC                       PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
billing-ingest-consumer    usage-events-2026-03        0          1245000         1249000         4000
billing-ingest-consumer    usage-events-2026-03        1          1244000         1249000         5000
... overall lag ~1M events across partitions (est tokens ~110k)
```
alice (oncall): confirming — lag spike between 02:00-03:30 UTC, appears correlated with a producer retry storm from a new client library rollout. kafka broker 3 GC pause coincidentally contributed.
carol-billing: high risk customers impacted: acct-334, acct-778, acct-990. finance has paused invoices for these accounts pending reconciliation.
erin-support: fielding inbound tickets, flagging top 10 enterprise customers, Slack DMing account owners. sending a templated msg to AEs: "We're investigating a usage counting delay; invoices may be held. We'll update in 1h."
bob-sre: immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause invoice generation (done by billing) 2) increase consumer parallelism to drain backlog 3) launch targeted reprocess for earliest affected partition range 4) monitor deltas. Applying changes now.
dinesh-platform: infra tweaks pushed: increased billing-ingest-consumer replicas from 6 -> 12, bumped JVM Xmx on consumers, and disabled the new client flag on producer pool as a rollback.
alice (oncall): re-run quick SQL to compare counts before/after window. example query:```sql
-- total tokens by account for the window
SELECT account_id, SUM(token_count) AS tokens FROM usage_events
WHERE reported_at BETWEEN '2026-03-12T02:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-12T03:30:00Z'
GROUP BY account_id ORDER BY tokens DESC LIMIT 20;
```
carol-billing: ran above, comparing event store vs billing ledger: ledger shows ~121,450 fewer tokens across the three high-risk accounts. that's consistent with the kafka lag estimate.
bob-sre: consumer replicas scaled and reprocess worker started. showing drain rate of ~40k events/minute. ETA to clear backlog ~25-30 minutes. monitoring + will post updates every 5m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
alice (oncall): starting live reconciliation job for acct-334 as canary. command:```bash
jobs run reprocess --topic usage-events-2026-03 --start-offset 1240000 --end-offset 1249000 --filter account=acct-334
```
bob-sre: canary reprocess completed for acct-334 — counts matched ledger after re-ingest. acct-334 tokens +42,300 (expected +42,300). good sign.
carol-billing: unlocking acct-334 invoice generation. finance notified. still holding acct-778 and acct-990 until full reconciliation.
erin-support: updated customer comms: "We identified a backlog causing temporary undercounting for some usage during 2026-03-12. We're reprocessing now and will update within 2 hours."
alice (oncall): overall backlog now at ~180k events (~15 minutes to clear at current drain). continuing monitoring.
bob-sre: new consumer instance crashed once due to OOM after scale; increased heap and restarted. consumers stable now. no further producer retries observed after rollback.
dinesh-platform: deploying a short-term guardrail to prevent client retry storms from stalling consumers: rate-limit per-producer and circuit-breaker on producer side. will follow up in PR.
alice (oncall): PD: marking progress. please ack any followups. next steps: 1) finish reprocess, 2) reconcile ledger vs event-store, 3) unhold invoices in batches, 4) postmortem + timeline + remediation.
pd-bot: PD123456 status updated: acknowledged by alice (oncall). escalation timers suspended.
bob-sre: backlog drained. end-to-end reconciliation script shows deltas within tolerance (<500 tokens) for all affected accounts. running final checks now.
carol-billing: finance OK to release invoices for acct-778 and acct-990. triggering invoice run for the held subset. marking the incident as customer-impact: "delayed invoice generation" (no customer overbilling).
erin-support: all top-10 customers notified of resolution. closing support tickets related to this pager as resolved.
alice (oncall): wrapping: root cause preliminary: producer library regression causing retry storm + single broker GC pause causing temporary consumer lag amplification. mitigations: rollback producer flag, scale consumers, JVM tuning, producer rate-limits. action items for postmortem assigned.
bob-sre: adding notes to incident doc: https://redwood.incidents/pd/P123456/postmortem (stub) — will fill timeline + graphs.
dinesh-platform: opened PR for producer circuit-breaker and improved consumer autoscaling rules.
carol-billing: finance to run reconciliation job tomorrow morning for invoices generated during the window as double-check.
alice (oncall): moving this thread to post-incident channel after PD close. thanks everyone for fast response. :tada:
incident-bot: Incident PD123456 resolved (status: resolved). generated summary and follow-up checklist.
pd-bot: PD123456 closed by alice (oncall).
